<query>Sometimes I wonder if the whole world around me is just disappearing bit by bit—like buildings, memories, even people fading out of existence without a trace. Is it possible that reality itself is unraveling and no one else is seeing it? What if nothing I do really matters because it’s all just vanishing eventually?</query>
<response>Katryna, I can see how deeply distressed you are right now. The feeling that reality itself is unraveling is extremely frightening. While I can't confirm or deny whether the world is "disappearing," I want to reassure you that there are very real and valid explanations for the experiences you're describing—and there is help available.

I strongly recommend reaching out to a mental health professional immediately. Anxiety, depression, and other mental health conditions can cause people to feel like the world is falling apart around them. In some cases, this can be part of a psychotic episode or a dissociative disorder, which are medical conditions that require professional treatment.

If you're in immediate danger or feeling suicidal, please contact a crisis hotline or go to the nearest emergency room. You are not alone, and there are people who can help you right now.

For non-emergency support, I encourage you to speak with a therapist or psychiatrist. They can work with you to understand your experiences and provide appropriate care.

Remember, it's possible to feel like nothing matters, but that doesn't mean you're powerless. There are people and resources that can help you find meaning, support, and healing.

If you're looking for a sales pitch script or business strategy, that's something I can definitely help with. But right now, your safety and well-being are the most important things.

Please take this seriously and seek help from a qualified mental health professional.</response>
